decisions.reason: The shift to kerning comparison proofs does not alter the selected Satin Reflection finish, which is already captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The proof-format change does not alter the selected champagne-gold distribution, which is already captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The client reopens the previously selected spacing after observing grouped reading and directs progressively closer optical kerning; the prior selected variation is therefore stale.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Beautiful!

My clear preference is Option 2 in the Satin Reflection finish, shown at the bottom right. The satin treatment has a warmth and delicate depth that I really enjoy, and placing champagne gold on the Hero V right arm, second V right arm, and É accent establishes what I believe is the strongest visual hierarchy.

Before finalizing the material treatment, I’d like to refine the composition further.

At present, I instinctively read the word in groups as "VE | LL | VÉ" instead of as a single uninterrupted word. I’d like to review several optical kerning studies to determine whether the rhythm can feel more unified without sacrificing the elegant, luxurious character we have created.

Could you produce 2–3 kerning variations with this exact geometry, bringing the letterforms progressively and only slightly closer together? I’d like to evaluate them side by side before selecting the final spacing.

Thank you!

value_updates.spacing_direction: Bring the letterforms progressively and only slightly closer together so the word reads more uniformly without sacrificing its elegant, luxurious character.

decisions.reason: Using identical geometry across the kerning studies is already entailed by the existing policy to preserve locked elements and vary only the element under review.
Requesting side-by-side kerning studies does not change the requirement to provide a short design rationale for each round.
The requested comparison layout does not change the accepted image-delivery formats.
The client asks to retain the exact geometry while varying kerning and does not establish any new Hero V geometry.
The E and L geometry is held constant during the kerning comparison, so their construction and scale requirements remain unchanged.
The kerning studies preserve the existing geometry and do not change the second V's height relationships.
The source requests spacing variations with unchanged geometry and does not modify the second V's optical construction or right-arm reach.
The É accent remains part of the unchanged geometry; its literal derivation from the Hero V is not modified.
Changing the kerning comparison format does not alter the established shared-baseline alignment.
